documentation: Durations, instants, marks and time sources are small Lua tables with metamethods (runtime/time.lua), so a + b, a < b and println(a) work without special code. Time sources use os.clock (CPU time) and os.time (whole seconds in real Lua).

declarations.name: Duration
declarations.documentation: A table holding whole nanoseconds, with metamethods for + - * / comparison and printing (1h 30m, 1.5s, -(1m 30s) ...), conversions and toComponents

declarations.name: seconds
declarations.documentation: 5.seconds, and the other unit properties (nanoseconds ... days) on Int, Long and Double

declarations.name: milliseconds
declarations.documentation: 250.milliseconds, and the other unit properties on Int, Long and Double

declarations.name: inWholeMilliseconds
declarations.documentation: inWhole* properties truncate toward zero, like Kotlin

declarations.name: measureTime
declarations.documentation: Runs the block and returns the os.clock time it took as a Duration

declarations.name: TimeSource
declarations.documentation: TimeSource.Monotonic reads os.clock, so it counts CPU time

declarations.name: AbstractDoubleTimeSource
declarations.documentation: Same as AbstractLongTimeSource but read() returns a Double (deprecated in Kotlin, so checked by a hand-written test)

declarations.name: AbstractLongTimeSource
declarations.documentation: Subclass it and override read(); markNow() converts through the DurationUnit passed to the constructor

declarations.name: Clock
declarations.documentation: Clock.System.now() reads os.time, so real Lua only has whole-second resolution

declarations.name: ComparableTimeMark
declarations.documentation: Marks from the same source compare with < > == and subtract to a Duration

declarations.name: DurationUnit
declarations.documentation: DurationUnit.SECONDS etc. are plain strings that the Duration functions look up

declarations.name: ExperimentalTime
declarations.documentation: An opt-in marker: annotations are skipped, so @OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class) is accepted

declarations.name: Instant
declarations.documentation: A table of epoch seconds plus nanoseconds, printed as an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp; supports + - Duration, Instant - Instant, comparisons, fromEpochSeconds, fromEpochMilliseconds, DISTANT_PAST and DISTANT_FUTURE

declarations.name: TestTimeSource
declarations.documentation: A manually advanced source: source += 5.seconds

declarations.name: TimedValue
declarations.documentation: A table with value and duration

declarations.name: TimeMark
declarations.documentation: A mark: elapsedNow(), hasPassedNow(), hasNotPassedNow(), + and - a Duration, and mark - mark

declarations.name: isDistantFuture
declarations.documentation: x.isDistantFuture

declarations.name: isDistantPast
declarations.documentation: x.isDistantPast

declarations.name: asClock
declarations.documentation: source.asClock(origin) gives a Clock that reports origin plus the time elapsed on the source

declarations.name: measureTimedValue
declarations.documentation: Returns the block result and its Duration; destructures as (value, duration)

declarations.name: times
declarations.documentation: 2 * 5.seconds: the Duration metamethod handles both operand orders

declarations.name: toDuration
declarations.documentation: n.toDuration(DurationUnit.X)

declarations.name: toDurationUnit
declarations.documentation: Returns the unit unchanged (a TimeUnit and a DurationUnit are the same string)

declarations.name: toJavaDuration
declarations.documentation: Returns the Duration itself: there is no separate java.time type

declarations.name: toJavaInstant
declarations.documentation: Returns the Instant itself: there is no separate java.time type

declarations.name: toJSDate
declarations.documentation: Returns the Instant itself: there is no JavaScript Date in Lua

declarations.name: toKotlinDuration
declarations.documentation: Returns the Duration itself: there is no separate java.time type

declarations.name: toKotlinInstant
declarations.documentation: Returns the Instant itself: there is no separate java.time type

declarations.name: toTimeUnit
declarations.documentation: Returns the unit unchanged (a TimeUnit and a DurationUnit are the same string)
